question: Article 6 of the proposal for a regulation on affordable housing (COM(2026)599) sets out criteria for identifying areas experiencing housing pressure, including for the purpose of adopting restrictive measures on short-term lettings and the use of residential properties.

The sources include the Mapadomo database, developed by the Joint Research Centre (JRC) and the Commission’s DG ECFIN, which contains data on property prices for calculating the price-to-income ratio – an indicator that compares house prices to annual net disposable income per capita. However, the database1 is currently undergoing maintenance, and no estimate has been given on when it might be available again.

The previous version contains data limited to the period 2000-2020. As a result, progress is being hindered on independent checks and simulations of the price-to-income ratio and the criteria for identifying areas with housing shortages, which affect the application of EU legislation. Against this backdrop: 1.
What are the reasons for the prolonged unavailability of the Mapadomo database, and when is it expected to be restored with up-to-date data?

What will the Commission do to ensure that data is accessible and simulations reproducible with a view to identifying areas experiencing housing pressure, with regard to the methodology for calculating the price-to-income ratio?
How will it provide an assessment of the effects of the regulation on affordable housing without the statistical bases used being made fully available to the public?
